title: What Interrupts the Next Bell?
subtitle: Random table · 1d6 situation spark · original table

fields.label: 1 · Unexpected ally
fields.value: An off-duty collector recognizes Nera and offers a lawful route through a closed door, but needs a witness for their own protection.

fields.label: 2 · Evidence changes hands
fields.value: The witness cylinder's buyer wants to resell it before leaving. Negotiate, follow or expose the sale; ownership is not proof of guilt.

fields.label: 3 · A route opens
fields.value: A stalled service lift exposes a crawlway to the Archive. The keeper will hold it for a practical favor, not an inevitable bribe.

fields.label: 4 · Danger announces itself
fields.value: A false beat reverses the upper bellwind. The warning gives skiff passengers time to land, tether up or choose the sheltered route.

fields.label: 5 · Competing priority
fields.value: Hospital staff ask for help separating the reserve before any shutdown. They can explain the relevant controls; this need not erase another solution.

fields.label: 6 · Faction disagreement
fields.value: The Unwritten's purist cell arrives with oil; its rescue wing asks the PCs to preserve the witness records. Decide which argument or alternative to offer.

fields.label: Use
fields.value: Roll one ordinary d6 when an interruption would help, or choose. Adapt to established facts; do not force a duplicate ally, contradict a secured clue or impose a player decision. Entries create opportunities, pressure and changes, not only punishment.
